title: GPS-LOGSOURCE: inverse-log half-root copies with polynomial memory

claims.statement: For every integer N>=2 and every fixed s in Z/NZ, the one algorithm GPS-LOGSOURCE in proof.md, with n=ceil(log2 N), L=log2 n, finite branch n<2^16384 and otherwise v=ceil(sqrt n), ell=ceil(log2 n), z=ceil(log2 ell), b=2*v*ell*(ell+4*z+32), m=ceil((n-1)/b), top-down trimmed widths and recomputed q0,G,K,H0,Qcap and both cutoffs recovers the entire secret with unconditional probability at least 1-2^-8 from independent ideal copies. On every execution branch, including failed attempts, discarded copies, incorrect labels, both abort cutoffs, initialization and cleanup, its total charged sequential work is T=O(2^(sqrt(n)*(log2 n)^2+sqrt(n)*(log2 n)^(9/8))). All constants are absolute and independent of N,s and outcomes; expressions with log2 n are used for n>=2 with the n=1 finite instance absorbed by an outside constant. The exact growth index of this full supported envelope is 1/2. These bounds and the fifth clean-input tolerance hold jointly for this same configuration.

All Q acquired source copies must be independent ideal coset states; no behavior is promised for malformed copies. This is a clean-input guarantee, not a proof that positive tolerance is impossible.
